Johnson–Trotter Algorithm

AlgorithmsCountingSequences
Game: List every ordering of a set by changing just one neighbouring pair at a time.
How to play: Step or run the algorithm and watch the largest "mobile" number move.
Look for the math

There is a way to list all permutations in which each one differs from the last by just one adjacent swap.

Mobile numbers

Each number looks left or right, written <k or k>. It is mobile if its neighbour in that direction is smaller. The algorithm swaps the largest mobile number with that neighbour, then reverses the directions of every larger number. Starting from <1 <2 … <n, it eventually reaches <2 <1 3> 4> … n>, where nothing is mobile.

A minimal-change order

Every new permutation is obtained by a single transposition of adjacent elements — the same idea behind Gray codes. The logic test checks for n = 1 through 7 that the algorithm produces exactly n! distinct permutations, that every step is one adjacent swap, and that it halts at the expected permutation.

Watch the largest number travel back and forth. What changes whenever it turns around?
